about: What the app relies on the Codex CLI doing, that a fake Codex CLI reproduces, for the minimum and pinned versions the
contract names. Each claim rests on the CLI itself: a sanitised real capture (P3.1, tests/fixtures/codex/cli/<version>/,
ANONYMISED.txt there), the app-server schema the CLI generated, a recorded observation of a real run, or the upstream
source at the release tag (tests/wp1/fixtures/codex-cli-source.json: tag, commit, file sha256, verbatim lines). What the
app's own code or plans say is recorded as an app assumption: it must agree, but it never backs a claim alone. Nothing
here is taken from a fake. tests/wp1/fake-cli-oracle.test.ts checks every entry against its sources (the real side)
and every fake against every entry it claims (the fake side).

rules.lines: A stream is split on line feeds (carriage returns dropped); blank lines are ignored.
rules.modes: exactly: the stream has exactly these lines, in order. inOrder: these lines occur in this order, other lines may sit between them. document: the whole stream is one JSON value.
rules.streams: stdout or stderr: the stream the real CLI uses. appReads names the streams the app accepts the lines on, when it is more tolerant than the CLI; the fakes are held to the real stream.
rules.matchers: exact: the line itself. regex: an anchored regular expression. rpcResult: a JSON-RPC answer with this id whose result has these fields. json: the document has these fields. {version} stands for the entry version (escaped inside a regex). sameFolderAsEnv: the value names the folder the variable names (the CLI canonicalises CODEX_HOME; the fakes echo it, and their virtual homes are already canonical, so they are compared exactly).
rules.exitCode: A number. Absent: not asserted, and a citation says why.
rules.afterwards: Then the named entry is run in the same realm and must hold too.
rules.kinds: upstream: verbatim lines of the release source, held in the upstream fixture. observation: a capture or a recorded real run (docs/wp2/evidence/, tests/fixtures/codex/). app-assumption: this app's source or plans; every path under src/ and the docs/wp2 plans is one.
rules.backing: For each version an entry covers, an asserted exit code, its lines, the stream of its lines and its afterwards must each be backed by a capture or schema of that version or by an upstream or observation citation; an app assumption never backs one alone. Every citation that backs a value must carry the entry value (so an app assumption that disagrees with the CLI is red). An upstream citation is checked against the fixture line by line, and its exit code, stream and samples against what those lines print and exit with.

Upstream lines the app does not read, and the wp1 FAKE prints differently, so no line claim: login --with-api-key prints "Reading API key from stdin..." and "Successfully logged in" on stderr (login.rs read_stdin_secret, run_login_with_api_key), the FAKE "Read key <key>" and "Successfully logged in" on stdout; logout prints "Successfully logged out" (or "Not logged in") on stderr (run_logout), the FAKE on stdout; a terminal on stdin gets "--with-api-key expects the API key on stdin. ..." on stderr, the FAKE "refuses a TTY". The app decides by the exit code and a status run afterwards (auth-operations.ts).
